This is a pre-produced programme comparison. Your search helped you find the programme; it did not personalize the comparison.

← Back to search

Maastricht Biomedical Sciences investigates health and disease from molecules and cells to organs and the whole human body. Students combine biological knowledge with laboratory work, data analysis, scientific communication and professional development. Restricted electives and a minor provide choice before an individual research internship and thesis.

Two qualified UCR alternatives retain a substantial biomedical core. One adds neurobiology, development and evidence-based research; the other combines biomedical science with general enterprise and product-development perspectives. Their whole-course structure differs from Maastricht’s integrated research, laboratory and professional assessments.

Academic year: 2026–2027

The 180 EC pathway has a 150 EC major and 30 EC minor or approved elective space. Three second-year restricted menus require one choice each; no fixed minor package is imposed. Progression, attendance, competence and elective-approval rules apply. The integrated internship, individual thesis and defence carry 22 EC, with additional entry requirements.

What this comparison shows

A curriculum-level comparison of Biomedical Sciences at Maastricht University with 2 illustrative UCR study compositions.

CLOSEST UCR MATCH
Biomedical mechanisms, health and research

Molecular and cellular biology, anatomy, physiology, pathology, immunity and pharmacology anchor this biomedical response. Neurobiology, development, mental health and systematic evidence synthesis add perspectives on health and disease. Research, statistics, data and image analysis support enquiry. These whole courses do not reproduce Maastricht’s integrated competency assessments or 22 EC internship and thesis.

ADDITIONAL UCR OPTION
Biomedical science and enterprise

The same substantial biomedical core, including laboratory work, anatomy, epidemiology and disease mechanisms, combines with enterprise, product design, marketing, accounting and governance. Research methods, statistics and data analysis support evidence-based work. Business courses contribute general methods and context; they do not establish biomedical product-development, clinical translation or regulatory training.

Important limitation

This is a curriculum comparison. A UCR composition is not the same disciplinary degree and does not by itself establish a professional qualification or automatic eligibility for a particular master’s programme.

Rows show curricular relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence. A blank cell means there is no closely comparable component in that row. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

modals.text:
Personal & Professional Development
This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
Close

Accounting & Corporate Finance
This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
Close

Consumer Product Design
You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
Close

Marketing & Consumer Engagement
Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer behaviour, brand strategy and responsible customer engagement. Students analyse case studies, develop marketing plans and consider digital and AI-driven changes in marketing.
Close

Strategy & Digital Transformation
The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.
Close

Market Research
See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.
Close

International Business & Governance
This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.
Close

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.
Close

Research Methods & Statistics
Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, sampling, experiments and surveys. Students study descriptive and inferential statistics, association, hypothesis testing and analysis of variance, with an introduction to multivariate applications. A group research project applies these methods to a chosen research problem.
Close

Introduction to Data Science
Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
Close

Image Processing & Computer Vision
Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how structural information is extracted from images and video. Topics include camera and colour models, filtering, edge and feature detection, segmentation, tracking and object recognition. Practical work develops computational image-analysis skills, with applications including medical imaging and remote sensing.
Close

Ethics
Ethics examines virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, alongside moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Students apply ethical arguments to issues including equality, poverty and wealth, animal rights, future generations, climate change and historical injustice. Papers and presentations develop independent argumentation.
Close

Qualitative Research Methodology
Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
Close

Epidemiology & Public Health
Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.
Close

Functional Anatomy
Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through surface anatomy, medical imaging, scientific drawing, dissection-related materials and clinical demonstrations. These are academic learning activities rather than clinical skills training.
Close

Pharmacology
Covers the science of drugs—their origin, composition, kinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity. Discusses drug targets, interactions and kinetics, enabling students to explain therapies in terms of molecular targets and physiological consequences.
Close

Infection & Immunity
Explores fundamental processes in immunology such as recognition of self vs non‑self, lymphocyte receptor development and innate and adaptive immune responses. Examines host‑pathogen interactions, inflammation, tissue damage and immunopathology.
Close

Mechanisms of Disease
Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. It connects embryology, anatomy and physiology with symptoms and failures in the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, digestive, endocrine and central nervous systems.
Close

Neurobiology
Neurobiology studies the biological basis of behaviour through evolutionary pressures, biorhythms, comparative anatomy, animal models and selected disorders. Students examine research ethics and animal welfare, practise laboratory techniques such as microscopy and cell staining, and compare brain anatomy across species.
Close

Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
Introduces cells, molecular biology, cellular physiology and communication. It connects genetic information and variation with living systems and offers initial perspectives on life sciences, biomedicine and public health. A research presentation develops engagement with scientific literature.
Close

Introduction to Brain & Behavior
Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
Close

Molecular Cell Biology
Provides foundation for practical applications in life science. Focuses on cellular biology of eukaryotes and prokaryotes, revisits concepts from introductory courses, examines current research and encourages evaluating reproducibility and modernising methods.
Close

Human Physiology
Studies normal functioning of the human body, covering structure‑function relationships, energy handling, homeostasis, signalling, organ systems and integration of their functions.
Close

Biochemistry
Explores the chemistry of life and biomolecules such as proteins, sugars, lipids and nucleic acids. Discusses metabolic pathways, the role of biomolecules in health and disease and applications in medicine, biotechnology and sustainability.
Close

Life Science Laboratory
Introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work. Covers themes like blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics and provides a foundation for clinical and biomedical research.
Close

Molecular Pathology & Genetics
Covers general and molecular pathology and genetics. Studies cell injury, death, inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, regeneration, fibrosis and neoplasia, examines genetic mutations and diseases, and discusses genetic testing and ethical considerations.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Abnormal Psychology
Provides a deep dive into factors shaping mental health. Teaches critical thinking, explores the bio‑psycho‑social approach and covers mental disorders, research findings and assessment techniques.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

Lifespan Developmental Psychology
Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
Close

Introduces biochemical and molecular laboratory work. Covers themes like blood, proteins, bacteria, DNA and bioinformatics and provides a foundation for clinical and biomedical research.
Close

Molecular Pathology & Genetics
Covers general and molecular pathology and genetics. Studies cell injury, death, inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, regeneration, fibrosis and neoplasia, examines genetic mutations and diseases, and discusses genetic testing and ethical considerations.
Close

Statistics & Experimental Methods
Teaches multivariate statistical methods for research on complex human phenomena. Topics include linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of variance and covariance, and non-parametric tests. Students select and apply models, assess statistical problems and report their analyses.
Close

Abnormal Psychology
Provides a deep dive into factors shaping mental health. Teaches critical thinking, explores the bio‑psycho‑social approach and covers mental disorders, research findings and assessment techniques.
Close

Advanced Research Seminar
Advanced Research Seminar introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.
Close

Lifespan Developmental Psychology
Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
Close

The Art of Rhetorical Communication
The Art of Rhetorical Communication develops rhetorical analysis, academic writing and oral presentation. Students examine classical Western roots and the canons of rhetoric, and learn to construct, organise and support persuasive arguments. Historical and contemporary examples connect rhetorical theory with practical communication.
